q: My husband and I have wondered why we did this. We love our baby girl. But it’s been SO MUCH HARDER than we ever thought.
cx: Eight weeks into a hard newborn stretch of feeding and crying problems.
r: unit: mental health and medical issues

q: But for those of you experiencing something that your mothers say, “well that didn’t happen to me,” I see you.
cx: What mothers of new mothers say when the newborn weeks are harder than theirs were.
r: unit: mental health and medical issues

q: Barely made it to week two when the infant dyschezia hit. Screaming for every poop. Pediatrician saying “anything that makes you gassy will make her gassy” (which is not based in any evidence).
cx: In week two, the paediatrician's diet advice that she followed without result.

q: FYI I have one of the lowest pain tolerance as a human being and if I could do it any one can.
cx: First-time mother three weeks after a 40-hour labour.

q: So thankful to the community and to all the posts here that made this journey so much more easy!
cx: She credits the forum's posts with easing her pregnancy.

q: I am a worry wart to the max and was breaking down the nights before from all of the things that could go wrong. If you want a peace of mind, here is my story.
cx: First-time mother recalls the nights before her induction, crying over what could go wrong.

q: I was terrified of this and all the things that could go wrong. Have your support person sit in front of you and you can grip their hand while the procedure happens.
cx: Her tip for the epidural she dreaded: hold the support person's hand.

q: Moral of my birth story: everything I worried about didn’t happen, and the worst part pain wise, was the bladder incident.
cx: Two days postpartum, her verdict on the fears before her induction.

q: We let my epidural wear off significantly so I could feel to push better, but it was worth it to know I was giving it everything I had.
cx: Before her labour ended in a caesarean, she wanted to know she had tried everything.
r: medication: epidural; newborn monitoring in unit

q: I love clothes and feeling like my clothing fits ME in size, lifestyle, and personality, so I definitely was crashing out for a minute there when things weren't fitting and I couldn't seem to put together an outfit that I liked.
cx: Early second trimester, nothing fitting and no outfit she liked.

q: Get the belly band that can go over your jeans pants asap. That bloating is going to come on quicker than you think and even your comfiest pants can feel too tight super fast. I wish I bought one earlier.
cx: Her first-trimester buying tip: a belly band, sooner than you think.

q: Why can't we have wide leg maternity jeans that aren't $90-200??
cx: Complaint that maternity jeans are mostly skinny, and wide-leg ones are $90-200.

q: I've had a good amount of luck with the Goodwill maternity section. I've had better luck there than at children's resale with maternity section.
cx: She buys maternity clothes second-hand at Goodwill.

q: I'm one of the first in my community to get pregnant, so that would never have occurred to me haha
cx: Told to borrow maternity clothes from friends, she says none of her friends have been pregnant.

q: A light weight, wedge style pregnancy pillow - I'm not one to go and buy a lot of things but this has definitely been with it, imo. I didn't buy the full pillow like others but just stuck with the wedge style one.
cx: At 36+5 after a rough pregnancy, the wedge pillow was worth buying.

q: A belly band! - This is one thing I truly wish I had night earlier in my pregnancy!
cx: She wishes she had bought a belly band earlier in pregnancy.

q: If you have any other suggestions, I'd also love to hear them as I'm always looking for ways to make my life less painful during pregnancy lol.
cx: Still asking for tips at 36 weeks.

q:
I’m unsure if anything can cure my exhaustion; however, things I love that have helped are   
\-Needed Electrolytes: I live in southern CA and the humidity and lingering heat has been killing me.
cx: Exhausted pregnant woman in a hot climate names the electrolyte brand that helps her.

q: That’s all, the rest is still shit lol. Stay strong soldiers
cx: Signing off her short list of what helps.

q: As a FTM, I wasn’t sure this was actually it (even though everyone told me I *would just know*!), especially since my water hadn’t broken.
cx: First-time UK mother on early contractions and what everyone had told her.

q: I called maternity triage, only to be told there was no bed at my local hospital and I’d need to go to another one 35mn away (bearing in mind my local one is just 5 mn away!).
cx: In labour, NHS triage first told her to go to a hospital 35 minutes away.
r: unit: unplanned birth before arrival, tear surgery

q:
*"This is early labour, it could be weeks before you give birth."*  
She told me to go home, ride it out, and take a hot bath.
cx: What the midwife said before sending her home; she gave birth at home hours later.
r: unit: unplanned birth before arrival, tear surgery

q: I remember distinctly telling my husband on the way back to the car: "If this isn’t labour, I don’t want to give birth anymore." 😂
cx: Sent home from hospital, what she said to her husband in the car park.

q: My husband rushed in to help and tried calling maternity triage and was** **put on hold for **17 minutes** while I cried out in pain on the toilet.
cx: Her husband was on hold to triage for 17 minutes as birth began at home.
r: unit: unplanned birth before arrival, tear surgery

q: I get really anxious when things are outside of my control and there are a lot of variables during labour so repeatedly told myself from the beginning that whatever happen will happen and as long as baby/me were okay it was the most important! This really helped with the whole ordeal.
cx: Advice to a pregnant commenter: the mantra she repeated through pregnancy.

q: My husband complained that he was tired from squeezing my hips which pissed me off lol. Other than that he was great 😂
cx: During labour, her husband's complaint about hip squeezes.

q: Was doing curb walking, eating dates, drinking the tea, etc.
cx: What she tried at the end of pregnancy before choosing induction at 41+1.

q: And in spite of the pregnancy, birth and recovery, I already know I want to do it all again.
cx: Five months after a hard birth and slow recovery.

q: I wanted to use hypobirthing techniques (from the positive birthing company book I read) and have as natural of a labour as possible.
cx: UK first-time mother prepared with a hypnobirthing book.

q: As i felt the urge to push, in the positive birthing company book, it tells you to ‘down breathe’ which i was doing but with every contraction, this didn’t really seem to do much to mine the labour along so i ended up needing to ditch this method and actually begin to push
cx: One hypnobirthing book technique she had to drop while pushing.

q: I call triage and they tell me to stay home as I’m a FTM and staying cosy at home is best at this stage
cx: NHS triage's repeated advice to stay home as a first-time mother; she was 8cm on arrival.

q: My husband was incredible at being the right levels of reassuring but also motivating. He kept me fed and hydrated, haribos were a lifesaver to give me the energy to keep going!
cx: Her husband's role in an unmedicated labour.

q: Within my 3rd trimester, I actually started to look forward to my labour and experiencing it all instead of fearing it - I believe this helped with my headspace.
cx: Her key takeaway: shifting from fear to looking forward to labour.

q: Everyone talks about preparing for labour and birth but I don’t think many people talk about the steps after birth and preparing for that. That includes the delivery of your placenta, any tears that require stitches, any significant blood loss and any injections you may need
cx: Two weeks postpartum, she names the gap: nobody prepares you for what happens right after the birth.
